title: Northstar - Vendor Risk & Commercial Approval Checkpoint

Action items include sharing an updated redline, SOC2/scoping doc, and pricing worksheet for executive approval; pilot to start after legal signoff.

Rita Gomez - Provide list of required audit artifacts and KMS constraints - 2026-09-04

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-02
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Tom (Northstar GC), Angela (Procurement), Marcus (Head of Platform), Rita (Security)

Summary (auto): quick checkpoint to close gating redlines, double-check SLA targets and pricing path.

[00:00] Maya: hi everyone thanks for squeezing this in, i'll kick off, uh, quick agenda — legal redlines, SLA numbers on dedicated/private, pricing approval path, next steps.
[00:18] Angela: hey Maya, thanks. we just want to be clear on who needs to see the MSA changes and what the timeline is for procurement escalation.
[00:26] Tom: yes and just to add - primary concern will be data residency and liability caps on the DPA, also encryption keys, we prefer bring-your-own-kms if possible.
[00:36] Maya: understood. from Redwood's side we support customer-managed keys for Private deployments, and Dedicated has KMS integrations too; i'll have Priya describe the technical pattern.
[00:44] Priya: hey, hi. so for Private we do a customer VPC control plane, keys stay in your KMS, we don't persist plaintext, and the audit logs can ship to your SIEM. small caveat — for some older model variants there are additional perf tuning steps because of quantization, but that's ops side.
[01:05] Marcus: can you clarify the perf implication — are we looking at 2x latency for quantized models? we need a baseline for acceptance criteria.
[01:12] Priya: it's workload dependent; typical chat 16k context on dedicated we see p95 around 200–300ms for smaller models, for quantized larger models can be 1.5x in some paths, but we can run a short benchmark during pilot and pin the metrics.
[01:29] Tom: that's useful, but liability caps — the DPA in our procurement portal flags an unlimited liability for some security incidents, that's a showstopper.
[01:37] Maya: got it. on liability we normally follow a capped liability framework per the MSA; we can surface the exceptions in the annotated redline. we'll propose a tiered cap tied to fees and breach severity.
[01:50] Angela: and then SLA — procurement's asking for a 99.95% monthly uptime target for the service. can you meet that on Dedicated?
[01:58] Priya: Dedicated is designed for predictable throughput; our SLA for Dedicated customers is typically 99.9% right now, but we do offer higher SLA tiers with reserved capacity and on-call escalation as an add-on. we can propose an enterprise SLA path in the redline.
[02:14] Rita: from security perspective we need SOC2 report and pen test summary, also proof of encryption-in-transit and at-rest with key management details. do you have a SOC2 Type II cert?
[02:24] Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II — i'll attach the SOC2 package and a high-level pen test summary. also we have a security pack link: https://redwood-inference.example/security-pack.pdf (note: placeholder).
[02:36] Tom: thanks. one more — data residency: certain PII must not leave eu-east region, are you able to pin region for inference?
[02:45] Priya: yes, region pinning is supported for Private and Dedicated in our EU regions. for hosted we have softer controls. if you need physical on-prem, we can look at the Private on-prem package but that raises the procurement ops conversation.
[02:58] Angela: pricing — procurement needs clarity on the committed spend, what triggers the overage, and a worksheet we can push to finance. can you give a sample deal structure?
[03:07] Maya: we usually propose a committed monthly spend for Dedicated with tiered unit pricing; there's an overage rate and an option for burst capacity. i'll send a pricing worksheet example; it will show committed baseline, burst, and quantization consult credits.
[03:20] Marcus: and how do rollouts work? we want canary and automatic fallback to lower-cost models if capacity spikes.
[03:27] Priya: rollouts supported — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible variants; routing policy can be by latency or cost. i'll include a one-pager on rollouts and the console screenshots.
[03:40] [background noise] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:44] Tom: legal also wants to know retention windows for logs — both audit logs and request/response. Northstar's policy is 90 days for request-level telemetry.
[03:53] Maya: we can conform to configurable retention; hosted default is 30 days but Dedicated and Private can be set to 90 or custom. we'll outline options in the DPA section.
[04:05] Rita: KMS question — can we hold the HSM root externally? our compliance says keys must be customer-controlled HSM.
[04:13] Priya: yes, customer-managed HSM supported in Private deployments; for Dedicated there are KMS integrations but not full HSM root separation unless it's a private on-prem deployment.
[04:27] Angela: procurement timeline: we're doing a monthly gating committee. if we get redlines back this week, we can push to the committee on 9/14, decision 9/21. can you meet that?
[04:36] Maya: timeline works — we'll aim to deliver the annotated MSA/DPA on 9/6 so you have time.
[04:42] Tom: how about indemnity language — we asked for mutual indemnities for IP claims.
[04:48] Maya: mutual IP indemnity is standard; if you have specific carve-outs please flag them in the redline.
[04:53] Marcus: ok great. about the pilot: we want a 4-week pilot, 2 sample workloads (embedding index and chat assistant), success metrics are throughput per dollar and p95 latency under a threshold.
[05:05] Priya: sounds good; we'll propose a pilot plan: week 0 baseline, week 1 ingest + perf runs, week 2 tuning, week 3 acceptance. will include scripts and a small benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:17] Angela: who signs the SOW for the pilot? procurement needs a short SOW with deliverables and acceptance criteria.
[05:24] Maya: we can attach a short pilot SOW to the agreement; i'll include scope, durations, success metrics and signoff steps.
[05:31] Tom: last commercial question — pricing approval: finance may need a revised TCO doc with 3-year view.
[05:39] Maya: we'll add a 3-year TCO model to the pricing worksheet.
[05:44] Rita: can you confirm whether request/response payloads are logged by default? we need an option to disable logging of full prompt/response.
[05:53] Priya: yes configurable; you can disable payload logging, keep only metadata and audit trails. we'll note that in the redline.
[06:02] Angela: ok, so immediate deliverables from Redwood for us to route to legal and procurement: annotated MSA/DPA, SOC2 pack, pen test summary, pricing worksheet + 3yr TCO, pilot SOW.
[06:13] Maya: correct. we'll deliver by 9/6. Priya will also add the technical runbook.
[06:19] [short pause]
[06:21] Tom: one more tiny note — can we get references of other financial customers who have done Private or Dedicated? that helps compliance.
[06:29] Maya: yes, we can provide anonymized references and case studies; i'll include a short reference list.
[06:35] Marcus: perfect. any blockers we didn't cover?
[06:38] Angela: timeline still looks tight but manageable.
[06:41] Maya: recap then: Redwood delivers annotated MSA/DPA + security pack + pricing worksheet and pilot SOW by 9/6. Northstar legal to prioritize redlines by 9/10. Procurement to gate committee 9/14. Pilot kickoff tentatively week of 9/20 pending legal. action items captured.
[06:58] Tom: thanks everyone.
[07:01] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up over email with documents and a calendar invite for the 9/6 review.
[07:08] Angela: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: pricing worksheet (link to be shared), SOC2 pack, annotated MSA redline, pilot SOW.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker id errors, 'KV cash' heard in one section instead of 'KV cache', small speech overlaps.
